reading.body:
This entry is a mapping error: E. D. Accounting Siena is an accounting firm with its own small server room, not a commercial data center, despite being tagged as one on OpenStreetMap.

Accounting practices maintain office computing systems and client financial servers as part of normal business operations. These internal IT closets serve a single firm's administrative needs. They differ categorically from commercial colocation facilities or cloud data centers, which aggregate compute resources across many customers and operate as standalone infrastructure businesses. The telecom=data_center tag applied here reflects confusion between a firm's own IT equipment and the type of facility that would anchor AI infrastructure.

This entry documents a determination rather than inventing specifications. The firm's name identifies its actual function plainly. No operator, website, or power consumption data exists because there is no commercial data center to record. The nearest airport and geographic coordinates mark the physical location, but they do not change what the site is.

OpenStreetMap's volunteer tagging system can apply infrastructure labels to office buildings that contain only routine IT closets. Distinguishing genuine commercial data centers from accounting offices that happen to have servers remains a practical problem for mapping AI's actual footprint.
